ARC-REV-01.rationale: No new domain rule is decided outside Tier 1/2. Hold queue order comes from Tier 2 Holds.queueFor. Branch membership and the unknown-branch error come from the existing Views.shelf, which calls Catalog.copiesAt. The member list comes from the existing Views.members projection. Tier 3 only sorts rows by id, as the export requires, and turns the existing DueBack projection into status text (presentation). The CLI only dispatches and renders.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: All new file writes go through the existing Files port. The change also removes an existing direct System.IO write from Tier 3 and keeps its behaviour. Nothing reads the clock or does I/O in Tier 1/2, and the CLI does not call Tier 2 directly.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Each fact used has one source. Inventory rows reuse the shelf projection (it gains a Book field rather than a second projection). Holds order reuses Holds.queueFor. The member export reuses the members view, whose type strings feed the import-members round trip. No limit, date rule or predicate is copied.

evidence.quote: let waitingFor bookId (library: Library) = queueFor bookId library |> List.length

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The holds-waiting count is defined in Tier 2 (Holds.waitingFor) and only projected in Views.shelf. Import validation of unknown or duplicate copies and books, and of unknown branches, is left to Tier 2 Catalog.addCopy and Catalog.findBranch. Tier 3 only parses CSV fields (boundary translation), numbers lines and folds the results into an all-or-nothing commit, which is orchestration.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The new file read uses the existing Files port, and persistence uses the existing commit/Store path. The Tier 2 addition is pure. The CLI only dispatches to UseCases.importCopies. The direct JsonFileStore use in the backup command (line 119) is existing context, not added by this change.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The holds-waiting count has one definition (Holds.waitingFor, built on queueFor), and the export reaches it through the shelf view. Copy, book and branch validity rules are referenced from Catalog, not restated. No domain literal or predicate is copied.
